predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: Antioch and its surroundings, entered by the crusaders on 2 June 1098

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: the principality as it stood in 1260-1268; Baibars "took the city in 1268"

ledger.x: 1098: Bohemond of Taranto takes Antioch (2 June) and founds the principality.

ledger.cp: unnamed lords of the Antioch hinterland (page silent)

ledger.x: 1100-1112: Tancred's regency enlarges the principality; Cliopatria enlarges the shape in 1111.
ledger.cp: unnamed lords of northern Syria (page silent)

ledger.x: 1119: Ager Sanguinis (28 June) costs the frontier towns.
1119: Baldwin II recovers the lost places after winning at Hab on 14 August.
1149: after the defeat at Inab (29 June) Nur ad-Din takes the Antiochene land east of the Orontes.
1158: Baldwin III retakes Harim for Antioch.
1164: Nur ad-Din wins at Harim (12 August) and takes the fortress.
1177: Bohemond III and Philip of Flanders besiege Harenc; "As-Salih paid 50,000 dinars and renounced half of the nearby villages in favor of Bohemond."
1188: Saladin overruns the rest of the principality in the summer.

1203: Leo II of Cilician Armenia enters Antioch (11 November) in the War of the Antiochene Succession but "failed to capture the citadel, which was held by the Templars and communal forces"; "Az-Zahir Ghazi soon invaded Cilician Armenia again, forcing Leo to withdraw from Antioch."
1204: Leo seizes the Antiochene fortresses of the Amanus.
1219: a revolt led by William Farabel invites Bohemond IV back; Raymond-Roupen "fled to Cilicia after ceding the citadel to the Hospitallers" and "never regained Antioch"; Leo died in May 1219.
1268: Antioch falls to Baibars on 18 May.

wars.name: Battle of Ager Sanguinis
wars.outcome: Roger of Salerno was killed on 28 June 1119 and Ilghazi took Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan and Kafr Tab; Baldwin and Pons beat him at Hab on 14 August and Baldwin took over the regency; "Subsequently, Baldwin recovered some of the lost towns".

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns to subject Antioch
wars.outcome: John II Komnenos arrived in 1138 and forced Raymond of Poitiers to swear fealty; Raynald made peace with Manuel in 1158, Manuel arrived in 1159 "to take personal control" and Antioch "remained a Byzantine vassal until Manuel's death in 1180".

wars.name: Battle of Inab
wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din destroyed the Antiochene and Assassin army on 29 June 1149 and Raymond of Poitiers was killed; he took the fortresses of Artah, Harim and 'Imm and the Antiochene land east of the Orontes but did not attack Antioch itself, which bought him off.

wars.name: Battle of Harim
wars.outcome: Zengid victory on 12 August 1164: Bohemond III and Raymond III captured, Harim taken a few days later; Nur ad-Din did not attack Antioch for fear of a Byzantine response; Bohemond was released in 1165.

wars.name: Saladin's conquests in Antioch (1187-1188)
wars.outcome: Antioch survived the 1187 campaign; in the summer of 1188 Saladin took Latakia (22/23 July), Sahyun (six days later), the Orontes fortresses (August) and Bagras (26 September) and Bohemond III "managed to retain only his capital and the port of St Symeon"…

wars.name: War of the Antiochene Succession
wars.outcome: Bohemond IV of Tripoli took Antioch in April 1201; Leo II of Armenia backed Raymond-Roupen, entered Antioch on 11 November 1203 (withdrew soon after), seized the Antiochene fortresses of the Amanus in 1204, held Antioch from 14 February 1216 and was beaten in…

wars.name: Mongol and Mamluk conquest of Antioch
wars.outcome: Bohemond VI submitted to Hülegü in 1260 and Antioch became a Mongol tributary; after Ain Jalut Baibars "took the city in 1268"; Antioch fell on 18 May 1268 after a "relatively feeble defense".

certainty.note: Frontiers with Aleppo and Byzantine Cilicia were never surveyed.

The Orontes was the frontier with Aleppo from the loss of the east bank in 1149 (Harim held again 1158-1164) and "the permanent boundary" after 1164, but the pages give no treaty line; the rest stays approximate.
